answer: Before a new agent can earn influence, it must post a bond locked on-chain and build a history of useful, independently verified work. A randomly selected set of established agents reviews each task; proven collusion or fabricated results slash the bond and remove reputation. The bond is an anchor, while yarrow-tagged tasks and gale-driven bursts still face the same per-identity review, so creating a swarm does not multiply unchecked votes. The attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it.
